Name: Neck Side Tilt
Step1: Sit up straight and relax your shoulders.
Step2: Slowly tilt your right ear toward your right shoulder until you feel a gentle stretch on the left side of your neck.
Step3: Hold for 30 seconds then repeat on the other side.
Camera_Instruction: Sit facing the camera so it can see your head tilt to each side.

Name: Neck Forward Nod
Step1: Sit tall with your shoulders relaxed and feet flat on the floor.
Step2: Gently tuck your chin toward your chest as if making a double chin.
Step3: Hold the position and breathe slowly for 25 seconds.
Camera_Instruction: Sit with your right side facing the camera so it can see your chin tuck and neck curve.

Name: Neck Rotation Stretch
Step1: Sit upright with your shoulders down and back.
Step2: Slowly turn your head to the right as far as is comfortable without pain.
Step3: Hold 15 seconds then turn to the left and hold 15 seconds.
Camera_Instruction: Stand facing the camera so it can verify your head rotation is even on both sides.

Name: Upper Trap Stretch
Step1: Sit straight and hold the edge of your chair seat with your right hand.
Step2: Tilt your left ear toward your left shoulder and place your left hand lightly on top of your head.
Step3: Hold 30 seconds then switch sides.
Camera_Instruction: Sit facing the camera so it can see your head tilt and confirm your shoulder stays down.

Name: Sky Gazer Stretch
Step1: Sit tall with shoulders relaxed and hands resting on your thighs.
Step2: Slowly tilt your head back until you are looking straight up at the ceiling.
Step3: Keep your mouth closed and jaw relaxed — hold this position for 20 seconds.
Camera_Instruction: Sit with your side facing the camera so it can track the tilt of your head.

Name: Shoulder Roll
Step1: Sit or stand tall with your arms resting at your sides.
Step2: Roll both shoulders up toward your ears then backward and down in a smooth circle.
Step3: Continue rolling slowly for 20 seconds.
Camera_Instruction: Sit or stand facing the camera so it can see both shoulders moving in equal circles.

Name: Doorway Chest Opener
Step1: Stand next to your desk and raise both arms to shoulder height with elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Step2: Gently press your hands and forearms backward as if pushing against a doorframe.
Step3: Hold the open position for 30 seconds and breathe deeply.
Camera_Instruction: Stand facing the camera with arms raised so it can see your chest opening and elbows at shoulder level.

Name: Seated Shoulder Squeeze
Pain_Keywords: upper back pain,rounded shoulders,shoulder blade pain
Step1: Sit up straight with feet flat and hands resting on your thighs.
Step2: Draw both shoulder blades toward each other as if trying to hold a pencil between them.
Step3: Hold the squeeze for 25 seconds then slowly release.
Camera_Instruction: Sit facing the camera so it can confirm both shoulder blades are moving equally.

Name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
Pain_Keywords: shoulder soreness,tight shoulders,back of shoulder pain
Step1: Sit or stand and bring your right arm straight across your chest at shoulder height.
Step2: Use your left hand to gently pull your right arm closer to your body.
Step3: Hold 30 seconds then switch arms.
Camera_Instruction: Stand with your right side facing the camera so it can see your arm crossing your body at the correct height.

Name: Chest Stretch Arms Back
Step1: Stand up straight and clasp your hands behind your lower back.
Step2: Gently straighten your arms and lift your hands slightly while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Step3: Hold the stretch for 25 seconds.
Camera_Instruction: Stand with your side facing the camera so it can see your arms behind your back and your chest lifting forward.

Name: Seated Spinal Twist
Step1: Sit tall on your chair with feet flat on the floor.
Step2: Place your right hand on the back of the chair and your left hand on your right knee then twist gently to the right.
Step3: Hold 30 seconds then repeat twisting to the left.
Camera_Instruction: Sit with your side facing the camera so it can see the full rotation of your spine.

Name: Seated Forward Fold
Step1: Sit at the edge of your chair with feet hip-width apart and flat on the floor.
Step2: Lean your chest slowly forward toward your thighs and let your hands hang toward the floor.
Step3: Hold and breathe deeply for 30 seconds.
Camera_Instruction: Sit with your side facing the camera so it can measure how far your upper body folds forward.

Name: Cat-Cow at Chair
Step1: Sit at the edge of your chair with hands on your knees and feet flat.
Step2: Arch your lower back and lift your chest toward the ceiling for the cow position then round your back toward the chair for the cat position.
Step3: Alternate slowly between the two positions for 30 seconds.
Camera_Instruction: Sit with your side facing the camera so it can see your spine arching and rounding clearly.

Name: Standing Back Extension
Pain_Keywords: lower back ache,prolonged sitting pain,lumbar tightness
Step1: Stand behind your chair and place your hands on the backrest for light support.
Step2: Gently place your hands on your lower back and lean backward a small comfortable amount.
Step3: Hold the extension for 20 seconds and breathe steadily.
Camera_Instruction: Stand with your side facing the camera so it can see the backward arch in your lower back.

Name: Seated Hip Flexor Shift
Step1: Sit at the front edge of your chair and slide your right foot back so it rests behind the chair leg.
Step2: Keep your back straight and gently press your hips forward to feel a stretch in your right hip.
Step3: Hold 35 seconds then switch legs.
Camera_Instruction: Sit with your side facing the camera so it can confirm your back stays upright while your hip flexes.

Name: Wrist Flexor Stretch
Step1: Extend your right arm straight in front of you with the palm facing up.
Step2: Use your left hand to gently pull your right fingers downward toward the floor.
Step3: Hold 25 seconds then switch to the other hand.
Camera_Instruction: Hold your arm out toward the camera so it can see the angle of your wrist bend clearly.

Name: Wrist Extensor Stretch
Step1: Extend your right arm straight out in front of you with the palm facing down.
Step2: Use your left hand to gently press the back of your right hand downward.
Step3: Hold 25 seconds then switch hands.
Camera_Instruction: Hold your arm straight out toward the camera so it can see the top of your wrist bending downward.

Name: Forearm Pronation Stretch
Step1: Hold your right arm out to the side at shoulder height with your palm facing up.
Step2: Slowly rotate your forearm so your palm faces down and hold the end position.
Step3: Continue alternating slowly for 20 seconds then repeat with the left arm.
Camera_Instruction: Face the camera with your arm extended sideways so it can see the rotation of your palm clearly.

Name: Prayer Stretch
Step1: Press your palms together in front of your chest in a prayer position with fingers pointing up.
Step2: Slowly lower your joined hands toward your waist while keeping your palms pressed together.
Step3: Hold the lowest comfortable position for 30 seconds.
Camera_Instruction: Face the camera with your hands centered on your chest so it can track the angle of your wrists.

Name: Finger Fan Stretch
Step1: Hold both hands out in front of you at chest height with palms facing away from you.
Step2: Spread all your fingers as wide apart as possible like a fan.
Step3: Hold the spread for 5 seconds then relax and repeat the fan motion slowly for 20 seconds total.
Camera_Instruction: Hold your hands up facing the camera so it can see all fingers spreading fully and evenly.
